_comment: How this language's phrases hold together, for lib/chunker.py. Optional, like every file of this name.
_why: Turkish is head-final throughout: the modifier before the noun (büyük ev), the case on the end of the word, the postposition after its noun (ev ile).
_verb_final: The verb comes last, so a noun before a verb is its object and leans toward it, and a noun after a verb begins a new clause (docs/lang/tr.md: end a chunk at the verb).

function_words._comment: The closed classes, which the dictionary is the wrong authority on: it gives `için` more senses as a noun and a verb than as the postposition it nearly always is, and `ona` as a numeral. A word under two headings is read in its place: `o ev` is a determiner, `o geldi` a pronoun.

_light_verbs: The verbs that make a verb of the noun before them, written apart and still one verb: `teşekkür ederim`, `yardım etmek`, `alışveriş yapmak`, `mutlu olmak` (docs/lang/tr.md: the noun of a compound belongs to its verb). Matched at the start of the word the dictionary calls a verb, or does not know.
